b: Causes: Most commonly Coxsackievirus B ( 1), but also uremia , post-MI , and autoimmune conditions.
Presents with pleuritic chest pain that is relieved by leaning forward.
Physical exam reveals a friction rub ; ECG shows diffuse saddle-shaped ST elevation .
Characterized by Beck's triad : hypotension + muffled heart sounds + JVD .
Also presents with pulsus paradoxus ( 10 mmHg drop in systolic BP with inspiration).
